title: Staying with his cabinet-maker uncle and the streetcar to the store
summary: Hirsch loved staying near the store with a cabinet-maker uncle, rode the streetcar down from Napoleon Avenue; another uncle was an actor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you live around Decatur and, uh, Frenchman ever?

No. I used to stay down there with them. I loved it down there because I was, my uncle, who I was very attached to, married to my aunt, my father's sister. And, uh, I loved it down there. I enjoyed it. My uncle was a, was a cabinet maker. And, uh, that's where I think I got my knowledge of cabinet making. And he was quite a guy. And, uh, I liked him very much. In fact, I used to, I lived up on Napoleon Avenue and Franklin, which is Napoleon Avenue, and Liberty now. Mm-hmm. Right. Not Liberty. I mean, uh, Warnsley. Warnsley, right. And, uh, I used to get on a streetcar, about a half a block from my house, for a nickel, and I'd be down at the store without transferring. Used to go, the Cronolet streetcar used to go, Cronolet, Napoleon Avenue, Cronolet, Cronolet, across Bourbon Street. Down Bourbon to Esplanade, across Esplanade to Decatur by the firehouse, and then down around that section, down Decatur Street. And went down Decatur Street. I don't know how, I don't remember how far it did, but I managed to get off the Frenchman in Decatur.
Did any of your, uh, uncles play music?
No. I had one uncle who was an actor.
He was a, a thespian. I gotta get it right. A thespian. He was, uh, he was quite a guy.
